::: {.callout-note}
## Data status: checked by a second extractor, draft analysis

Every secondary-outcome row was checked against the source PDFs by a second extractor on 10 November 2026 (worklist `verification_worklist_secondary_2026-11-10.xlsx`; the check and the decisions it led to are in the decision log, `Status.md`). Of `r nrow(sec)` trial-by-outcome rows, `r sum(sec$fit_all)` enter the pooled fits, `r sum(sec$status == "descriptive")` are descriptive only (one arm not reported) and `r sum(sec$status == "excluded")` are excluded. Open items: (1) for Confalonieri 2005, new septic shock, the denominators are 23/23 as reported, kept for simplicity; patients with septic shock at entry cannot develop new shock, and Tables 1 and 2 imply 21 patients at risk in each arm (Table 1: 2 hydrocortisone and 1 placebo patient in shock at entry; Table 2 prints 9 (43%) in the placebo group), but the fit with 21/21 gives the same pooled result (OR 0.53) (the row is flagged `denominator_as_reported`); (2) the window is not stated for seven rows (flagged `window_unstated`); (3) Torres 2015 is included in all five outcomes using its supplement (obtained 10 November 2026): combined 0 to 120 h counts for new ventilation (5/61 vs 9/59) and new septic shock (2/61 vs 7/59) from eFigure 1, and both arms for GI bleeding and super-infection from eTable 8. Its denominators are the intention-to-treat numbers as reported; for septic shock the at-risk denominators would be 51 and 41 (eTable 3), which gives the same result (OR 0.47 against 0.48 in all trials). The analysis is a draft and the secondary outcomes do not override the mortality conclusion.
:::

The protocol (PROSPERO field 25) lists secondary outcomes to be summarised descriptively and, where the data allow, with the same Bayesian framework, without overriding the mortality conclusion. Following the approved plan (`SECONDARY_OUTCOMES_PLAN.md`, rules R1–R7):

- **Pooled outcomes:** five binary outcomes across all included trials: secondary infection, GI bleeding, hyperglycaemia, new invasive ventilation and new septic shock.
- **Severe-only fits:** the same analysis restricted to the primary set, for new septic shock, secondary infection and GI bleeding.
- **One row per trial:** chosen by fixed timepoint rules. For harms, the window closest to day 28; for progression outcomes, the latest window within 30 days.
- **Hyperglycaemia:** each trial's own definition, preferring "requiring treatment" where both are reported.
- **Model:** the same as for mortality: exact binomial likelihood, unpooled trial baselines, reference prior N(0, 1) on the log-OR, τ ~ half-Normal(0, 0.5).

For harms, the probability that corticosteroids increase the event, P(OR > 1), is the quantity of interest; for new ventilation and new septic shock, P(OR < 1) is.

## Pooled results

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sec-main
ss |>
  mutate(ord = match(outcome, names(sec_outcome_label))) |>
  arrange(ord, set != "all", variant != "main") |>
  transmute(Outcome = sec_outcome_label[outcome],
            Analysis = paste0(ifelse(set == "all", "All included", "Severe-only"),
                              case_when(variant == "no_long" ~ ", long windows dropped",
                                        variant == "treated" ~ ", treated definition only", TRUE ~ "")),
            Trials = n_trials,
            `Events, steroid` = sprintf("%d/%d", events_s, n_s), `Events, control` = sprintf("%d/%d", events_c, n_c),
            `OR (95% CrI)` = or_ci(OR_median, OR_q025, OR_q975),
            `P(OR>1)` = pr(P_OR_gt_1), `P(OR<1)` = pr(P_OR_lt_1), `tau median` = pr(tau_median),
            `Predictive OR, new trial` = or_ci(ORnew_median, ORnew_q025, ORnew_q975)) |>
  kable(caption = "Secondary outcomes, reference prior N(0, 1). Rows checked by a second extractor (10 November 2026); draft analysis. OR < 1 favours corticosteroids (fewer events).")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sec
#| fig-cap: "Pooled odds ratios for the secondary outcomes (posterior median and 95% credible interval), all included trials and severe-only.. Rows checked by a second extractor (10 November 2026); draft analysis."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(mutate(main, Outcome = factor(sec_outcome_label[outcome], rev(sec_outcome_label)),
              Analysis = ifelse(set == "all", "All included trials", "Severe-only (primary set)")),
       aes(OR_median, Outcome, xmin = OR_q025, xmax = OR_q975, colour = Analysis)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  geom_pointrange(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Odds ratio, corticosteroid vs control (log scale)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

All `r nrow(sd_tab)` secondary-outcome fits `r if (all(sd_tab$pass)) "pass" else "do not all pass"` the acceptance rules used for mortality (R-hat below 1.01, bulk and tail ESS above 400, no divergences). The largest R-hat is `r sprintf("%.3f", max(sd_tab$max_rhat))` and the smallest bulk ESS `r round(min(sd_tab$min_ess_bulk))`.

Points to keep in mind when reading these results:

- **Few trials.** Each fit rests on 3 to 10 trials, so τ is poorly identified and the predictive intervals are wide.
- **Definitions and windows differ.** The trials define the outcomes differently and report them over different windows. This is why the timepoint rules and the long-window and treated-definition sensitivity fits exist.
- **Hyperglycaemia mixes definitions.** It combines "any hyperglycaemia" (very common in shock trials) with "hyperglycaemia requiring treatment", so its pooled OR is an average over different definitions. The treated-only fit is the cleaner comparison.

## Rows used

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sec-rows
sec |>
  filter(fit_all == 1) |>
  mutate(ord = match(outcome, names(sec_outcome_label)),
         raw_or = ((r1 + 0.5) / (n1 - r1 + 0.5)) / ((r0 + 0.5) / (n0 - r0 + 0.5))) |>
  arrange(ord, final_set, study_label) |>
  transmute(Outcome = sec_outcome_label[outcome], Trial = study_label, Set = final_set, Timepoint = timepoint,
            Definition = definition, Steroid = sprintf("%d/%d", r1, n1), Control = sprintf("%d/%d", r0, n0),
            `Raw OR (0.5 added, display only)` = pr(raw_or), `Severe-only fit` = ifelse(fit_severe == 1, "yes", ""),
            Flags = coalesce(sensitivity_flags, "")) |>
  kable(caption = "Rows entering the pooled fits (from analysis_secondary.csv). The raw OR adds 0.5 to every cell for display only; the model uses the exact counts.")
```

## Rows not pooled

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sec-other
sec |>
  filter(fit_all == 0) |>
  mutate(ord = match(outcome, names(sec_outcome_label))) |>
  arrange(ord, study_label) |>
  transmute(Outcome = sec_outcome_label[outcome], Trial = study_label, Status = status,
            Steroid = ifelse(is.na(r1), "–", sprintf("%s/%s", r1, n1)),
            Control = ifelse(is.na(r0), "not reported", sprintf("%s/%s", r0, n0)),
            Reason = decision) |>
  kable(caption = "Rows left out of the fits: descriptive only (one arm not reported) or excluded.")
```

The continuous secondary outcomes (hospital and ICU length of stay, ventilator-free days, ventilation duration, time to clinical stability) and the sparse binary outcomes (readmission, ICU admission, ARDS, delirium, neuromuscular weakness, serious adverse events, treatment failure) will be reported descriptively, as the plan specifies. That table is still to be added.
